consequences: Frontend never talks directly to NATS
adrs.context: The canonical architecture requires UI to Caddy to FastAPI before NATS, workers, agents, supervisors, and evidence.
adrs.decision: Browser-facing control and command admission remain behind FastAPI rather than exposing execution backplanes to the PWA.
runtime_implications: FastAPI availability is part of write readiness
security_implications: Backend secrets remain outside the browser
adrs.title: FastAPI owns the browser-facing control API

consequences: Prepared projections may be stale while durable state remains authoritative
Operational health and semantic parity remain independent
adrs.context: The architecture model distinguishes durable-state components from projections and requires truthful reconciliation.
adrs.decision: Durable control-plane records remain in SQLite while prepared projections optimize bounded reads.
runtime_implications: Projection freshness can gate writes without deleting durable history
adrs.title: SQLite is durable authority for control-plane state
trade_offs: Preserves durable recovery and auditable state

alternatives: FastAPI directly managing remote device processes
consequences: Restart Agent progress must reflect actual delivery and recovery
Supervisor absence produces guidance rather than fake repair
adrs.context: The canonical architecture separates command execution, reconnect recovery, and stopped-agent recovery.
adrs.decision: Joined-device execution stays in the node agent and recovery stays in a separate supervisor/watchdog path.
runtime_implications: Running-but-disconnected and stopped-agent recovery remain distinct
security_implications: Protected agent identity stays on the managed device
adrs.title: Agents and supervisors own device execution and recovery
trade_offs: Keeps remote execution local to the managed device

adrs.context: Device onboarding must fail closed on identity mismatch and prevent duplicate or protected-host enrollment conflicts.
adrs.decision: Device invites and bootstrap commands are generated by backend services after duplicate and identity checks.
runtime_implications: Identity mismatches fail before environment or PM2 mutation
security_implications: Invite/bootstrap secrets are not exported into documentation
adrs.title: Bootstrap artifacts are backend-generated and identity-guarded
trade_offs: Prevents browser-held enrollment secrets and unsafe identity overwrite

alternatives: Generate tracked docs directly from the current phone
consequences: Observed does not automatically mean verified
Promotion preflight fails closed on binding or semantic mismatches
adrs.context: Runtime verification has backend, Termux, desktop, and mobile lanes and promotion is release- and source-bound.
adrs.decision: Tracked runtime documentation consumes sanitized promoted baselines, not arbitrary transient captures.
runtime_implications: Documentation generation does not mutate runtime state
security_implications: Transient raw capture stays outside tracked outputs
adrs.title: Runtime evidence is explicitly promoted
trade_offs: Promotion is an explicit operator step
Tracked documentation stays deterministic, sanitized, and reviewable

alternatives: One global frontend store for backend truth
adrs.context: The frontend must remain responsive without becoming an execution engine or durable backend authority.
adrs.decision: TanStack Query owns live server-state reads, Dexie stores safe read-only snapshots, Zustand owns harmless UI coordination, and XState owns guided workflow state.
runtime_implications: Saved state never proves current operational health
security_implications: Safe snapshots exclude secrets and write responses
adrs.title: Frontend state libraries have distinct ownership

glossary.definition: The server-side canonical state that survives process restarts and is authoritative over derived projections.
A bounded read model derived from authoritative state for fast UI/API reads; it may become stale without replacing durable authority.
Sanitized runtime evidence explicitly bound to a release and source commit and accepted through the promotion gate.
A user-facing representation that differs textually from backend values but is explicitly allowlisted as semantically equivalent.
Agreement of intended meaning across canonical backend, API, runtime, and presentation lanes under declared comparators.
Current runtime ability of a subsystem to serve reads, accept safe writes, recover, and maintain required connectivity independently of semantic parity.
One bounded observation source such as backend, Termux, desktop browser, or mobile browser used for runtime verification.
The verified association among release tag, source commit, runtime evidence, and release metadata.
An architecture boundary where trust level, credentials, validation, or execution ownership changes.
A restore preview recent enough to satisfy write-safety guards before a destructive restore.
An explicit device enrollment path used after identity ownership changes; it is not an automatic overwrite.
An explicit recovery action that preserves identity and backend ownership rather than silently mutating enrolled state.

accepted-limitation.meaning: A known constraint is explicitly accepted for a bounded scope.

contract-derived.does_not_prove: The contract was exercised successfully at runtime.
contract-derived.meaning: The fact is derived from a generated or canonical contract such as OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, or parity metadata.

degraded.meaning: Operational runtime health is reduced or a safe read/write guard is active.

healthy.does_not_prove: Release readiness or complete semantic parity.
healthy.meaning: Available runtime health signals satisfy the current health policy.

not-applicable.meaning: The field or condition has no applicable runtime object for the observed scenario.

not-observed.meaning: The required or optional runtime fact was not captured in the evidence lane.

observed.does_not_prove: Semantic agreement with another lane or operational health.
observed.meaning: A runtime lane successfully captured the field or state.

partial.does_not_prove: Failure of the portions that are implemented.
partial.meaning: The capability or domain is not fully implemented or not fully verified.

planned.meaning: The model intentionally reserves a future capability that is not implemented as current truth.

ready-with-accepted-limitations.meaning: Readiness may proceed while explicitly tracked limitations remain accepted.

release-promoted.does_not_prove: All domains are verified or operationally healthy.
release-promoted.meaning: Evidence was explicitly promoted and bound to a release/source identity.

runtime-observed.meaning: A runtime observation contributed to the knowledge fact.

source-derived.meaning: The fact is deterministically derived from repository-owned source or canonical metadata.

unvalidated.meaning: Implementation or metadata exists without the evidence required for validation.

verified.does_not_prove: Every underlying subsystem is currently operationally healthy.
verified.meaning: Appropriate contract or runtime evidence confirms the expected semantic condition.

verified-with-mapped-presentation.does_not_prove: Literal string equality between backend and UI.
verified-with-mapped-presentation.meaning: Backend/runtime meaning is verified while the frontend uses an explicitly allowlisted user-facing representation.
